subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should deferred context-engine maintenance adopt this opt-in lane-release-and-fence contract, or should core use an existing host safety budget with a cooperative cancellation contract instead?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but source review cannot decide whether a new public configuration key, generic queue callback, and intentionally abandoned plugin worker are the permanent product and plugin-lifecycle contract.

options.title: Define host-owned cancellation
options.body: Refactor the fix around one existing or owner-approved host safety budget and a cooperative maintenance abort contract before merging.

options.title: Accept opt-in fencing
options.body: Approve the new configuration and queue callback as the supported contract, documenting that plugin work may continue after lane release.

options.title: Pause the timeout change
options.body: Land only independently useful stalled-warning throttling and defer the timeout behavior until the context-engine lifecycle is explicitly designed.

recommendation.title: Define host-owned cancellation
recommendation.body: Refactor the fix around one existing or owner-approved host safety budget and a cooperative maintenance abort contract before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history indicates that jalehman introduced the context-engine integration and is the strongest available owner for its timeout and cancellation contract.
